issues.explanation: The Threat node is not clinically coherent as selected. These three items are not threat appraisals or threat-related cognitions; they are general PTSD symptoms spanning arousal, dissociation/re-experiencing, and concentration problems. Within-node, they do not express a shared threat meaning. Cross-node, the formulation shows Threat has only a very weak link to Memory and no active links to other nodes, yet the selected Threat items are largely memory/re-experiencing and hyperarousal phenomena rather than a distinct sense of current threat. This makes the Threat component inconsistent with both node content and formulation structure.

issues.item: Threat: Flashbacks: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
issues.explanation: These Threat items are not clinically coherent with the rest of the profile. Flashbacks is a re-experiencing/memory phenomenon rather than a threat appraisal item, and it duplicates the very strong Memory node, which already contains multiple intense reliving items. Irritability is also not a threat cognition and does not connect plausibly to the formulation, where Threat has only a very weak edge to Memory and no active links to Negative Appraisals. In contrast, the selected Negative Appraisals and Memory items form a coherent mutually reinforcing pattern. Hypervigilance is compatible with terrorism trauma, but the Threat node as a whole is internally inconsistent because its items mix a memory symptom, an arousal symptom, and a threat-monitoring symptom rather than a coherent threat representation.
